<!-- Generated by `bun run docs:reference` from seek's definitions. Do not edit. -->

The settings seek reads, generated from their JSON Schema definitions: one schema for the client configuration and one for the server configuration, which share the secret, provider and Vault shapes.

## Names

Each setting's environment variable is `SEEK_` followed by its YAML path in upper case, with dots and hyphens replaced by underscores, and its flag is `--` followed by its path with dots replaced by hyphens. A `value` has an environment variable and no flag, a boolean flag also has a `--no-` form, and a `command` array is written as a JSON array. `--config` and `SEEK_CONFIG` name the one configuration file to read in place of the default files.

## Secret sources

Where seek reads one secret. Set exactly one of `value`, `file`, `command` or `vault`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | The secret itself, with surrounding whitespace removed. `seek config show` prints it as `<redacted>`. It has an environment variable and no flag. |
| `file` | string | Path of a file that holds the secret, such as a container secret mount or a systemd credential. seek removes surrounding whitespace from its content. A leading `~/` is the home directory; another relative path in a configuration file is relative to that file's directory. |
| `command` | array of string | A credential helper and its arguments, as an array. seek runs it without a shell, in the directory of the configuration file that declared it, and reads the secret from its standard output, trimmed. A non-zero exit status is a failure. Errors and `seek config show` name only the program, its first element, and the number of arguments. As an environment variable or flag, the array is JSON. |
| `timeout` | string | How long seek waits for the helper before it stops it and fails. |
| `vault` | object | One field of a Vault or OpenBao KV secret. `path` and `key` are required. Each other field it leaves unset takes the merged top-level `vault` setting. |

## seek client configuration

The client configuration, read by every seek command except `seek serve`: `/etc/seek/client.yml`, then `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/seek/client.yml` (`~/.config/seek/client.yml` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset, empty or relative), which overrides it. `--config <path>` or `SEEK_CONFIG` names one file in place of both. Each field also has an environment variable and a flag, derived from its path as the configuration specification describes.

Definition: [configuration.client.schema.json](configuration.client.schema.json) (JSON Schema 2020-12), with the shared shapes in [configuration.secrets.schema.json](configuration.secrets.schema.json).

### seek client configuration settings

| Setting | Type | Accepted values | Default | Environment | Flag | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.url` | string | A URI, or empty |  | `SEEK_SERVER_URL` | `--server-url` | Base URL of a seek server. When it is set, the CLI sends every provider call to `<url>/v1/proxy/<upstream>` with the client token and does not use `providers`. Trailing slashes are removed. An empty value turns server mode off. Inspection and errors print it with any user name, password, query or fragment replaced by `<redacted>`. |
| `vault.address` | string (uri) | Matches `^(https?://[^/@?#]+(/[^?#]*)?\|unix:///[^?#]+)$` |  | `SEEK_VAULT_ADDRESS`, `BAO_ADDR`, `VAULT_ADDR` | `--vault-address` | Address of the Vault or OpenBao server: an `https://` or `http://` URL, which may end in a base path such as `/team-a`, or `unix://` followed by the absolute path of a socket. It carries no user name, password, query or fragment. Trailing slashes are removed, and request routes are appended under the base path. |
| `vault.namespace` | string |  |  | `SEEK_VAULT_NAMESPACE`, `BAO_NAMESPACE`, `VAULT_NAMESPACE` | `--vault-namespace` | Vault or OpenBao namespace, sent as the `X-Vault-Namespace` header. An empty string selects the root namespace: no header is sent, and no top-level or exported namespace is filled in. |
| `vault.mount` | string | Matches `^/*(?!\.\.?(/\|$))[^/]+(/(?!\.\.?(/\|$))[^/]+)*/*$` | `secret` | `SEEK_VAULT_MOUNT` | `--vault-mount` | Mount of the KV secrets engine. Leading and trailing slashes are removed; an empty, `.` or `..` segment is invalid. |
| `vault.kv-version` | integer | `1`, `2` | `2` | `SEEK_VAULT_KV_VERSION` | `--vault-kv-version` | Version of the KV secrets engine. |
| `vault.ca-cert` | string |  |  | `SEEK_VAULT_CA_CERT` | `--vault-ca-cert` | Path of a PEM bundle of the certificate authorities seek trusts for this server. It replaces Bun's whole default store: its bundled roots, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and, with `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1`, the system store. A leading `~/` is the home directory; another relative path in a configuration file is relative to that file's directory. |
| `vault.proxy` | string (uri) | Matches `^https?://[^/@?#]+/?$` |  | `SEEK_VAULT_PROXY` | `--vault-proxy` | HTTP proxy for this server's requests, as an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host and optional port only; it carries no user name, password, path, query or fragment, and seek sends no proxy credentials, as the operator decided in `authenticated-vault-proxy`. Without it seek connects directly and ignores `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`. |

### seek client configuration secrets

Each secret is one source mapping, and `vault.auth` is one `auth` mapping; a higher layer replaces either whole. The fields of each are listed below with their environment variables and flags.

| Setting | Environment aliases | Stdin flag | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.token` |  | `--server-token-stdin` | The client token the CLI sends to the seek server as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is one token. The CLI reads it only when a command calls the server. |
| `providers.parallel.api-key` |  | `--providers-parallel-api-key-stdin` | Parallel API key, used by `seek web parallel`, `seek research parallel` and `seek scrape parallel`, and sent to Parallel as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `providers.exa.api-key` |  | `--providers-exa-api-key-stdin` | Exa API key, used by `seek web exa` and `seek scrape exa`, and sent to Exa as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `providers.brave-search.api-key` |  | `--providers-brave-search-api-key-stdin` | Brave Search API key, used by `seek web brave search`, and sent to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `providers.brave-answers.api-key` |  | `--providers-brave-answers-api-key-stdin` | Brave Answers API key, used by `seek web brave answers`, `seek research brave` and the Brave planner of `seek research google --interactive`, and sent to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `providers.perplexity.api-key` |  | `--providers-perplexity-api-key-stdin` | Perplexity API key, used by `seek web perplexity`, `seek research perplexity` and the Perplexity planner of `seek research google --interactive`, and sent to Perplexity as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `providers.google.api-key` |  | `--providers-google-api-key-stdin` | Google Gemini API key, used by `seek research google`, and sent to Google as the `x-goog-api-key` header. |
| `providers.firecrawl.api-key` |  | `--providers-firecrawl-api-key-stdin` | Firecrawl API key, used by `seek scrape firecrawl`, and sent to Firecrawl as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `vault.auth` | `BAO_TOKEN`, `VAULT_TOKEN` |  | How seek authenticates to the server. `mode` selects the method and is required. An `auth` mapping is used only for the server in effect where it was declared, as the configuration specification describes. |

## seek server configuration

The server configuration, read by `seek serve`: `/etc/seek/server.yml`. `--config <path>` or `SEEK_CONFIG` names another file in its place. Each field also has an environment variable and a flag, derived from its path as the configuration specification describes.

Definition: [configuration.server.schema.json](configuration.server.schema.json) (JSON Schema 2020-12), with the shared shapes in [configuration.secrets.schema.json](configuration.secrets.schema.json).

### seek server configuration settings

| Setting | Type | Accepted values | Default | Environment | Flag | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.host` | string |  | `127.0.0.1` | `SEEK_SERVER_HOST` | `--server-host`, `--host` | Interface the server binds. The server image sets `SEEK_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0`. |
| `server.port` | integer |  | `8787` | `SEEK_SERVER_PORT` | `--server-port`, `--port` | Port the server listens on. |
| `server.require-token` | boolean |  | `true` | `SEEK_SERVER_REQUIRE_TOKEN` | `--server-require-token`, `--no-server-require-token`, `--no-auth` | Whether a request must carry one of `server.tokens`. Set it to false only on a trusted network; the server then logs a warning at startup. |
| `server.secret-refresh-seconds` | number |  | `300` | `SEEK_SERVER_SECRET_REFRESH_SECONDS` | `--server-secret-refresh-seconds` | How long the server uses each secret it resolved before it resolves it again. A later resolution that fails keeps the value already held. Zero resolves on every use. |
| `vault.address` | string (uri) | Matches `^(https?://[^/@?#]+(/[^?#]*)?\|unix:///[^?#]+)$` |  | `SEEK_VAULT_ADDRESS`, `BAO_ADDR`, `VAULT_ADDR` | `--vault-address` | Address of the Vault or OpenBao server: an `https://` or `http://` URL, which may end in a base path such as `/team-a`, or `unix://` followed by the absolute path of a socket. It carries no user name, password, query or fragment. Trailing slashes are removed, and request routes are appended under the base path. |
| `vault.namespace` | string |  |  | `SEEK_VAULT_NAMESPACE`, `BAO_NAMESPACE`, `VAULT_NAMESPACE` | `--vault-namespace` | Vault or OpenBao namespace, sent as the `X-Vault-Namespace` header. An empty string selects the root namespace: no header is sent, and no top-level or exported namespace is filled in. |
| `vault.mount` | string | Matches `^/*(?!\.\.?(/\|$))[^/]+(/(?!\.\.?(/\|$))[^/]+)*/*$` | `secret` | `SEEK_VAULT_MOUNT` | `--vault-mount` | Mount of the KV secrets engine. Leading and trailing slashes are removed; an empty, `.` or `..` segment is invalid. |
| `vault.kv-version` | integer | `1`, `2` | `2` | `SEEK_VAULT_KV_VERSION` | `--vault-kv-version` | Version of the KV secrets engine. |
| `vault.ca-cert` | string |  |  | `SEEK_VAULT_CA_CERT` | `--vault-ca-cert` | Path of a PEM bundle of the certificate authorities seek trusts for this server. It replaces Bun's whole default store: its bundled roots, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and, with `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1`, the system store. A leading `~/` is the home directory; another relative path in a configuration file is relative to that file's directory. |
| `vault.proxy` | string (uri) | Matches `^https?://[^/@?#]+/?$` |  | `SEEK_VAULT_PROXY` | `--vault-proxy` | HTTP proxy for this server's requests, as an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host and optional port only; it carries no user name, password, path, query or fragment, and seek sends no proxy credentials, as the operator decided in `authenticated-vault-proxy`. Without it seek connects directly and ignores `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`. |

### seek server configuration secrets

Each secret is one source mapping, and `vault.auth` is one `auth` mapping; a higher layer replaces either whole. The fields of each are listed below with their environment variables and flags.

| Setting | Environment aliases | Stdin flag | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.tokens` |  | `--server-tokens-stdin` | The client tokens the server accepts, as one comma-separated value, so that a new token can be added before the old one is removed. Required while `server.require-token` is true. |
| `providers.parallel.api-key` |  | `--providers-parallel-api-key-stdin` | Parallel API key, used by `seek web parallel`, `seek research parallel` and `seek scrape parallel`, and sent to Parallel as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `providers.exa.api-key` |  | `--providers-exa-api-key-stdin` | Exa API key, used by `seek web exa` and `seek scrape exa`, and sent to Exa as the `x-api-key` header. |
| `providers.brave-search.api-key` |  | `--providers-brave-search-api-key-stdin` | Brave Search API key, used by `seek web brave search`, and sent to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `providers.brave-answers.api-key` |  | `--providers-brave-answers-api-key-stdin` | Brave Answers API key, used by `seek web brave answers`, `seek research brave` and the Brave planner of `seek research google --interactive`, and sent to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header. |
| `providers.perplexity.api-key` |  | `--providers-perplexity-api-key-stdin` | Perplexity API key, used by `seek web perplexity`, `seek research perplexity` and the Perplexity planner of `seek research google --interactive`, and sent to Perplexity as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `providers.google.api-key` |  | `--providers-google-api-key-stdin` | Google Gemini API key, used by `seek research google`, and sent to Google as the `x-goog-api-key` header. |
| `providers.firecrawl.api-key` |  | `--providers-firecrawl-api-key-stdin` | Firecrawl API key, used by `seek scrape firecrawl`, and sent to Firecrawl as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. |
| `vault.auth` | `BAO_TOKEN`, `VAULT_TOKEN` |  | How seek authenticates to the server. `mode` selects the method and is required. An `auth` mapping is used only for the server in effect where it was declared, as the configuration specification describes. |

## seek config show --json

What `seek config show --json` prints: the effective client or server configuration, one entry per setting, with the layer that supplied it. Secrets appear as their configured source, never as their value. It is the supported interface for scripts that read seek's configuration.

Definition: [configuration.show.schema.json](configuration.show.schema.json) (JSON Schema 2020-12).

| Field | Type | Accepted values | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `configuration` | any | `client`, `server` | Yes | Which configuration was inspected. |
| `files` | array of string |  | Yes | Absolute paths of the configuration files that were loaded, from lowest to highest precedence. |
| `settings` | array of any |  | Yes | Every setting the configuration's schema defines, in schema order. A secret is one entry at the path of its source mapping, the top-level Vault login is one entry at `vault.auth`, and every other setting is one entry at its own path. |
| `warnings` | array of string |  | Yes | Warnings that loading wrote to stderr, such as a deprecated key and the key that replaces it. |
